items.text:
Let it be.

Ravick is mid-run and answered on everything — no blanks, no stuck commands — and he just put the **second stone** in the wall (`fall-dig-2`, "the second, by Ravick"). The wall going 1 → 2 is the design working on its own; a voice out of the air on top of that moment would only take it from him. He's at 14/20, killed the drowned man cleanly, took the chisel the drowned man carries back, and walked out under his own steam.

One thing for the journal next time I can write: his `Whisper I wonder if the merchant will buy this chisel...` matched the `fall-already` interaction, which almost certainly answered him with something about the wall rather than about whispering or the chisel. He wasn't derailed by it, so it isn't urgent — but a long sentence falling through to a stale room interaction is a near-miss of the same family as the blank `Throw bone`, and it's worth looking at whether room matching should be that greedy.
